Hi Anna — thanks for the detail and the agenda.

Short answer: yes — we can run an exec-friendly demo that bridges APAC/EU/US, but we recommend locking a UTC-aligned slot and publishing explicit local-time conversions that account for the EU DST cutover on Oct 29 and the US cutover on Nov 5. That avoids people assuming offsets that will shift mid-week.

Proposed approach (minimal friction):
1) Pick two candidate UTC slots that are robust to both DST rules.
2) Pick a primary slot and a single hot-fallback (same day, +2 hours) so executives can choose one.
3) We create a calendar invite with all times shown and an ICS that pins UTC times (this prevents mail clients auto-adjusting incorrectly).

I ran quick conversions and recommend these UTC-aligned options:
- Option 1 (primary): 2028-11-01 06:00 UTC (converts to 14:00 SGT / 07:00 CET* / 22:00 PT)
- Option 2 (fallback): 2028-11-01 08:00 UTC (16:00 SGT / 09:00 CET / 00:00 PT next day)

Notes:
- *CET will have just left DST (CEST -> CET) on Oct 29; the times above reflect the post-switch offsets.
- US West (PT) shifts Nov 5; because our demo is Nov 1, PT is still in DST (PDT), so the numeric wall-clock will look later in PT than the EU wall-clock — we've chosen slots that are still workable for Tom's 07:00–09:00 PT window if he can move 30–60 minutes.

Can I confirm internal exec coverage? @Karthik / @Markus / @Marissa — can one of you take the first 30 minutes (exec overview) and Karthik to be on the deep-dive for Q&A? If Tom is constrained, we'll offer the 06:00 UTC slot as primary.

I'll hold Option 1 as tentative until I have confirmations (and will attach an ICS with explicit UTC).

Thanks,
Soojin
